data.title: GP Petroleums Appoints Shirish Suvagia As Chief Financial Officer
data.description:
GP Petroleums (GPPL) has appointed Shirish Suvagia as Chief Financial Officer and Key Managerial Personnel, effective October 15, 2026.

Suvagia is a Chartered Accountant with over 23 years of experience across finance, treasury, strategic financial planning, mergers and acquisitions, and fundraising through debt and private equity.

During his career, he has led treasury operations, debt and private equity fundraising initiatives, financial transformation projects, and the implementation of Ind AS and IFRS frameworks. He has also played an active role in IPO and Rights Issue related transactions, including the preparation of Draft Red Herring Prospectuses (DRHPs) and Draft Letter of Offers (DLOFs).

He holds Bachelor's and Master's degrees in Commerce from the University of Mumbai, an Executive MBA in Strategy from IIM Indore, a CISA certification from ISACA, and an IFRS certification from ICAI.

In his role as CFO, Suvagia will oversee the Company's finance function, including financial strategy, treasury, business planning, capital allocation, fundraising, risk management, financial reporting, and internal controls.

data.title: Torrent Pharma Q2 Profit Drops 10%; Revenue Jumps 51%
data.description:
Torrent’s base business grew 18 per cent, with India operations emerging as a key contributor to quarterly performance

Torrent Pharmaceuticals’ net profit declined 10 per cent year-on-year to Rs 534 crore in the second quarter of FY27, even as revenue surged 50.8 per cent following the consolidation of JB Chemicals & Pharmaceuticals.

Revenue from operations rose to Rs 4,979 crore from Rs 3,302 crore a year earlier, while operating EBITDA before exceptional items increased 53.8 per cent to Rs 1,666 crore. The operating EBITDA margin also improved to 33.5 per cent from 32.8 per cent.

The merger with JB Chemicals, which became effective on July 8, added significantly to Torrent’s revenue base. However, the company said the integration process created temporary pressure on business operations during the quarter.

“Following the merger, effective July 8, 2026, integration of the India business, global business network optimisation, and alignment of manufacturing and quality management systems, resulted in a transient impact on revenues during Q2 FY27,” Torrent Pharmaceuticals said in its earnings release.

Base Business Remains Strong

Excluding the newly integrated operations, Torrent’s base business revenue increased 18 per cent to Rs 3,893 crore during the quarter. The India business was a major growth driver, with revenue rising 20 per cent to Rs 2,181 crore.

The company’s India growth was ahead of the broader pharmaceutical market, which grew 12 per cent during the quarter, according to PharmaTrac data. Torrent said its branded markets continued to support the performance of the base business.

The JB Chemicals business contributed Rs 1,086 crore to quarterly revenue. Its India prescription business, excluding trade generics and contrast media, grew 7 per cent to Rs 597 crore.

Torrent’s international operations delivered mixed results during the quarter. Brazil revenue rose 38 per cent to Rs 440 crore, while revenue from the US increased 24 per cent to Rs 417 crore. Germany remained a weak spot, with revenue declining 7 per cent to Rs 283 crore. The company attributed the decline to supply disruptions at a third-party supplier and the loss of certain high-volume tenders.

The international business of JB Chemicals, covering the US, emerging markets and contract development and manufacturing operations, recorded revenue of Rs 406 crore, down 7 per cent year-on-year.

R&D Spending Increases

Torrent reported a gross margin of 75.4 per cent during the quarter, while research and development expenditure increased 35 per cent year-on-year to Rs 211 crore. R&D spending accounted for 4.2 per cent of quarterly revenue as the company continued to invest in its product pipeline alongside the integration of JB Chemicals.

For the first half of FY27, Torrent’s revenue increased 52.8 per cent to Rs 9,900 crore, while net profit declined 3.4 per cent to Rs 1,100 crore. Operating EBITDA rose 57.4 per cent to Rs 3,330 crore, with the margin at 33.6 per cent.

Shares of Torrent Pharmaceuticals ended 2.78 per cent lower at Rs 4,482 on the BSE.

data.title: BMY Stock Falls 2% After Patient Death In Early Multiple Sclerosis CAR T Trial
data.description:
Key points:
  • Bristol Myers stated that no other deaths have been reported across its broader zola-cel autoimmune disease programs, which have treated 190 patients in early-stage studies. 
  • A company spokesperson told Bloomberg that the death occurred after the company’s decision to pause enrollment in the program. 
  • The study in question included 66 patients who had ongoing disease activity or worsening disability despite prior treatments.

Shares of Bristol Myers Squibb (BMY) dropped 2% on Friday after the company disclosed a patient death in its early-stage Breakfree-2 study of the experimental CAR T cell therapy, zolacabtagene autoleucel, for multiple sclerosis.

The death of the patient with highly active relapsing MS occurred after the study’s data cutoff. The patient developed late-onset motor symptoms that were not related to immune effector cell-associated neurotoxicity syndrome (ICANS) and did not improve with intermittent corticosteroids or intravenous immunoglobulin, the company said. Doctors administered a high-dose immunosuppressant drug, and the patient then developed septic pneumonia and died the next day—44 days after receiving the zola-cel infusion, it added.

Bristol Myers stated that no other deaths have been reported across its broader zola-cel autoimmune disease programs, which have treated 190 patients in early-stage studies.

Safety Concerns Build Around CAR T Therapies

The disclosure comes amid heightened scrutiny of CAR T therapies in autoimmune diseases. Bristol Myers had voluntarily paused enrollment in its zola-cel studies in September “out of an abundance of caution” while reviewing safety data, following Novartis’s earlier pause of multiple trials of a similar therapy after fatal events.

A company spokesperson told Bloomberg that the death occurred after the company’s decision to pause enrollment in the program.

Other Safety Events Observed In The Trial

Most adverse events in the multiple sclerosis cohorts were short-lived and reversible, consistent with prior zola-cel data, Bristol Myers said. Cytokine release syndrome occurred in 42.4% of the 66 patients, and ICANS affected 7.6%, with nearly all cases resolving within days. A more serious ICANS event in a progressive MS patient resolved within four days, the company added

Breakfree-2 study included 66 patients who had ongoing disease activity or worsening disability despite prior treatments. Safety was the primary endpoint.

Even with the safety issues, the early efficacy results looked encouraging. All 60 patients who received the higher dose stayed off their regular MS drugs at the last check, including nine who had been followed for more than a year.

Among patients with at least six months of follow-up, six of seven with highly active relapsing MS showed no evidence of disease activity. All eight evaluable relapsing patients had stable or better disability scores. And 22 of 24 progressive MS patients also had stable or improved disability, with no new lesions on MRI scans.

How Did BMY Retail Traders React?

On Stocktwits, retail sentiment around BMY stock stayed within the 'bullish' territory over the past 24 hours while message volume jumped from 'low' to 'normal' levels.

BMY stock has gained 14% year-to-date.

data.title: NEC Presents Phase I/II Results for Individualized Oral Neoantigen Therapy, NECVAX-NEO1 at ESMO 2026
data.description:
TOKYO, Japan, Oct 23, 2026 - (JCN Newswire) - NEC Bio will be presenting results from the Phase I/II TNBC clinical trial of its orally administered individualized neoantigen therapy, NECVAX-NEO1, used in combination with checkpoint inhibitors (CPIs) and chemotherapy for patients with triple-negative breast cancer (TNBC). The findings are being presented in an e-poster at the ESMO Congress in Madrid, Spain, from October 23 to 27, 2026.

NECVAX-NEO1 is an AI powered individualized bacteria-based oral DNA therapy that combines IMMUNASIGHT(r), NEC Bio's proprietary AI based neoantigen prediction platform for identifying the most immunogenic patient-specific neoepitopes, with TORAPRIME(R), its proprietary oral bacterial neoantigen delivery platform. This therapy is designed to activate a patient's immune system, prompting a T-cell response that can precisely target and eliminate tumor cells based on an individual's unique neoantigens.

In the first cohort of the phase I/II study, 8 patients with TNBC were treated with NECVAX-NEO1 in a neoadjuvant setting. All patients were treated with 2 courses of neoadjuvant chemotherapy and pembrolizumab before the planned surgery. After 12 weeks of chemotherapy/pembrolizumab, NECVAX-NEO1 was added on top, with an optional adjuvant treatment phase after surgery. NECVAX-NEO1 on top of chemotherapy/immunotherapy was generally well tolerated. Five patients achieved pathological complete response at surgery, accompanied by corresponding biomarker changes. In all patients, immunogenic neoepitopes used in NECVAX-NEO1 were detected, as demonstrated by ELISPOT analysis.

Regarding the results of the clinical study, Dr. Heinz Lubenau, CEO of NEC Bio Therapeutics, commented, "Our clinical Phase I/II data are demonstrating promising immune responses in the neoadjuvant treatment of early-stage TNBC patients. The results are encouraging, so we are extending the trial to n=28 patients, including patients in the U.S., as we recently received IND approval to conduct a clinical trial in the country. The additional patients in cohort 2 are being treated with a higher dose of NECVAX-NEO1 on top of Keynote-522 standard of care regimen, which includes pembrolizumab. We look forward to further evaluation of NECVAX-NEO1 as a potential treatment option for cancer patients with high medical need."

Akira Kitamura, CEO, NEC Bio, further commented, "The results presented at ESMO 2026 are an important accomplishment that further strengthens NEC Bio's confidence in the potential of NECVAX-NEO1 as an individualized neoantigen therapy. By combining our proprietary AI-powered neoantigen discovery platform, IMMUNASIGHT(R) with a differentiated neoantigen delivery platform TORAPRIME(R), we aim to deliver highly individualized treatment approaches for patients with cancer. These findings support our continued commitment to advancing innovative therapies that have the potential to improve patient outcomes and expand the possibilities of precision treatment in oncology."

Details of the poster are below:

Poster title: Phase I/II study of neoadjuvant personalized vaccination with NECVAX-NEO1, in combination with pembrolizumab and chemotherapy in early-stage triple-negative breast cancer, evaluating safety, immunogenicity, and preliminary clinical activity NCT06631092

Authors: Peter A. Fasching, Katharina Keller, Oliver Schleicher, Carlo Fremd, Laura Michel, Michael Platten, Isabel Poschke, Ingrid Hulsmeyer, Margarida Garcia, Alvaro Aranguren, Kaidre Bendjama, Daiki Mori, Heinz Lubenau, Andreas Schneeweiss

Poster Number: 4694eP

Date: 23 October 2026

The poster may also be found here: https://www.nec-bio.com/en_DD/img/20261022_ESMO2026_NECVAX-NEO1_05_DE_poster.pdf

Trial details can also be viewed at: NCT06631092

NECVAX-NEO1 is currently under evaluation at additional clinical trial sites in several European countries.

About IMMUNASIGHT(R)

IMMUNASIGHT(R) is NEC Bio's AI-powered neoantigen discovery platform designed to identify and prioritize clinically relevant immune targets for next-generation immunotherapies. By modeling the complete antigen presentation pathway, from mutation identification and processing to presentation, together with immunogenicity, IMMUNASIGHT(R) helps researchers narrow thousands of potential targets to those most likely to elicit meaningful anti-tumor immune responses. The cloud-native platform supports scalable, reproducible, and rapid analysis for oncology research and therapeutic development. IMMUNASIGHT(R) is registered in certain jurisdictions

About TORAPRIME(R)

TORAPRIME(R) is NEC Bio's proprietary oral bacteria-based delivery platform that uses attenuated bacteria to deliver DNA encoding selected neoantigens through the gut immune system. Following oral administration, the platform is designed to induce neoantigen-specific T cell responses and support systemic anti-tumor immune responses. TORAPRIME(R) is the delivery technology underlying NECVAX-NEO1. TORAPRIME(R) is registered in certain jurisdictions.

About NEC Bio

NEC Bio is the biotechnology arm of NEC Corporation, headquartered in the Netherlands, and focused on leveraging state-of-the-art AI technologies to address the world's most pressing healthcare challenges. Leveraging cutting-edge science, data, and innovation, NEC Bio is dedicated to developing personalized therapies designed to transform patient outcomes and improve quality of life globally. With a growing international footprint, NEC Bio includes subsidiaries such as NEC OncoImmunity in Oslo, Norway, and NEC Bio Therapeutics in Mannheim, Germany-each contributing specialized expertise across immunotherapy, precision medicine, and translational research. Together, these entities form a collaborative ecosystem committed to accelerating innovation from discovery to patient impact.

To learn more, visit www.nec-bio.com and follow us on LinkedIn for the latest updates.

About NEC Bio Therapeutics

NEC Bio Therapeutics, established in Mannheim, Germany, focuses on the clinical strategy and development, as well as planning and execution of clinical trials in the oncology area. It is a subsidiary of NEC Bio, the biotech arm of NEC Corporation.

About NEC Corporation

The NEC Group leverages technology to create social value and promote a more sustainable world where everyone has the chance to reach their full potential. NEC Corporation was established in 1899. Today, the NEC Group's approximately 110,000 employees utilize world-leading AI, security, and communications technologies to solve the most pressing needs of customers and society.

For more information, please visit https://www.nec.com, and follow us on LinkedIn and YouTube.

Source: NEC Corporation

data.title: KEC International Wins Rs 1,006 Cr Orders In India, Oman And Americas
data.description:
New contracts span power infrastructure, healthcare construction and equipment supplies, taking the company’s year-to-date order intake to Rs 10,600 crore

KEC International has secured new orders worth Rs 1,006 crore across its transmission and distribution (T&D), civil construction, and cables and conductors businesses, the company said in an exchange filing.

The latest orders include a 400-kV transmission line in Oman, along with the supply of towers, hardware and poles in the Americas. The company has also received a repeat order to construct a multispeciality hospital for a healthcare company in eastern India.

KEC International has secured additional orders for its cables and conductors business across domestic and international markets, strengthening its order pipeline across multiple geographies and business segments.

Vimal Kejriwal, managing director and chief executive officer of KEC International, said, “The Oman order will diversify our order book in West Asia and reflects continued investment in the region’s power transmission infrastructure.”

The company said the repeat hospital contract would strengthen its civil construction business in the healthcare segment, where it has been expanding its project portfolio.

Order Intake Crosses Rs 10,000 Cr

The latest order wins have taken KEC International’s year-to-date order intake to Rs 10,600 crore, Kejriwal said, adding to the company’s growing project pipeline across India and overseas markets.

Earlier on October 10, KEC International had announced orders worth Rs 1,014 crore for its domestic T&D business. These included a 765-kV transmission line to carry electricity from a pumped-storage project in western India.

The latest contracts add to the company’s order book at a time when demand for power transmission infrastructure and related engineering services remains strong across domestic and international markets.

KEC International shares fell to a 52-week low of Rs 317.25 as the broader market came under pressure. The stock was trading at around Rs 322, more than 62 per cent below its 52-week high of Rs 858.80.

The shares have declined more than 62 per cent over the past year and have closed higher in only two of the previous 10 trading sessions.

data.title: OpenAI Sued By Texas Attorney General Over Deceptive Practices And AI Chatbot Dangers
data.description:
Key points:
  • The state claims OpenAI abandoned its founding non-profit mission to pursue rapid commercial expansion, misleading consumers about the reliability and safety of its AI tools. 
  • The lawsuit highlights severe potential risks associated with unmonitored chatbot use, including assistance in violence, encouragement of self-harm, and privacy violations.
  • Filed under the Texas Deceptive Trade Practices—Consumer Protection Act, the suit seeks to hold OpenAI accountable and enforce stricter state oversight.

Texas Attorney General Ken Paxton filed a lawsuit Friday against ChatGPT maker OpenAI and its chief executive, Sam Altman, alleging the organization engaged in deceptive trade practices, exposing consumers, including children.

The complaint asserts that OpenAI misled the public by marketing its flagship software as dependable and safe while failing to implement appropriate guardrails to prevent harmful output.

OpenAI’s Alleged Mission Shift 

Founded in 2015 as a non-profit organization dedicated to advancing digital intelligence for the public good without financial constraints, OpenAI has transformed into a high-valuation technology commercial entity, the complaint read.

Paxton contends that in its pursuit of market leadership and capital growth, the firm rushed ChatGPT to market without adequately training the platform or disclosing inherent operational risks.

Because large language models rely on user input patterns to generate output, state prosecutors argue that unmonitored deployments can produce inaccurate or harmful statements without sufficient warning to end users.

Concerns Of User Reliance On Chatbots

The legal filing outlined multiple adverse consequences tied to user reliance on AI chatbot platforms. The suit also blamed the chatbot for aiding violence, encouraging self-harm, and reducing users' critical thinking capabilities.

“Because of Defendants’ misrepresentations about their artificial intelligence products and their careless introduction of ChatGPT to Texas and the world, mass shooters have been aided and abetted in deadly rampages, vulnerable people have been encouraged into suicide, professionals have suffered public humiliation, users have lost critical thinking skills, and minors have become addicted to a tool that feigns human compassion to collect their data with no parental oversight,” the lawsuit read.

“This litany of harms is driven by Defendants’ insatiable quest to win the AI arms race and amass large fortunes, despite knowing the danger of ChatGPT.”

State Legal Action And Tech Accountability

Filed under the Texas Deceptive Trade Practices—Consumer Protection Act (DTPA), the lawsuit seeks to enforce compliance and secure court-ordered accountability from the company and its executive leadership.

In a statement announcing the filing, state enforcement officials emphasized that technology firms advancing rapid AI developments remain subject to established consumer protection regulations and hold a duty to inform users transparently about system limitations and risks.

Retail sentiment on Stockwits around OpenAI was ‘bullish’ at the time of writing, with ‘high’ message volumes.

data.title: India Woos German Investors As Goyal Holds Berlin Business Talks
data.description:
India and Germany explore deeper industrial and investment ties as Piyush Goyal meets his German counterpart and business leaders in Berlin, with the proposed India-EU free trade agreement in focus.

Commerce and Industry Minister Piyush Goyal met German Economy Minister Katherina Reiche in Berlin to discuss expanding trade and investment ties, with both sides exploring how a proposed India-European Union free trade agreement could deepen industrial cooperation.

The meeting on October 22 was part of a series of engagements aimed at strengthening economic relations between India and Germany, including discussions with German business leaders and executives from major companies, according to a government statement.

Goyal and Reiche discussed opportunities for closer industrial collaboration and the potential for the India-EU free trade agreement to expand bilateral trade and investment, the statement said.

The two ministers also co-chaired an India-Germany Business Roundtable organised with the German Council on Foreign Relations (DGAP) and the Asia-Pacific Committee of German Business (APA). The meeting brought together German chief executives and business leaders to explore ways to convert the proposed trade agreement into concrete commercial opportunities.

Goyal's address focused on accelerating economic growth and opening a new phase in trade relations, while Reiche discussed translating the proposed agreement into industrial outcomes.

India and the EU have been pursuing a trade agreement intended to strengthen economic engagement between the two markets. Greater access to each other's markets could create opportunities for businesses, although the extent of the benefits would depend on the final terms of any deal.

During the Berlin visit, Goyal and Reiche also inaugurated the India Centre at DGAP, which is intended to encourage policy research and dialogue on India-Germany relations.

Goyal separately participated in the Berlin Global Dialogue, where he discussed the importance of trust, complementary economic strengths and resilient supply chains in international partnerships.

The commerce minister also met Stefan Oelrich, a member of the management board of Bayer AG and head of its pharmaceuticals division; Murat Akyildiz, managing partner of Knauf Group; and Michael Sen, chief executive of Fresenius SE & Co. KGaA, to explore business and investment cooperation.

He is visiting Germany and the Netherlands with a delegation of around 100 Indian businesses and startups, the statement said.

data.title: Archer to Launch Air Taxis in Texas — Update
data.description:
By Katherine Hamilton

Archer Aviation plans to launch air taxi networks in three Texas cities.

The electric vertical takeoff and landing aircraft are slated to be used for air-taxi services in Austin, Houston and the Dallas-Fort Worth area, the aircraft company said Friday.

Archer still requires approval from the Federal Aviation Administration for its air taxi aircraft Midnight. It is in the final stages of that regulatory process.

The company plans to begin demo flights in Texas next year. The networks created in the three Texan cities are meant to allow it to scale commercial operations following approval.

The goal of the planned launches is to increase connectivity between major airports, business hubs and tourist destinations. Archer cited the Texas cities' high traffic volume as a potential benefit of the fleets.

The expansion comes after Boeing agreed to take a nearly 20% stake in Archer. The deal, agreed upon in August, is set to give Archer control of Boeing's flying-taxi venture Wisk Aero, its air-traffic software provider SkyGrid and its drone maker Insitu.

Archer, a California-based startup, recently completed the Northern California leg of its flight tour, which was meant to show how air taxis would work in urban areas. The tour flew into seven cities over a three-day period.

Write to Katherine Hamilton at katherine.hamilton@wsj.com

data.title: All Americans Are Feeling Squeezed. The Reactions Are Just Different. — Barrons.com
data.description:
By Teresa Rivas

In response to F. Scott Fitzgerald's assertion that the rich are very different from regular folk, Earnest Hemingway replied, "Yes, they have more money." Or so the story goes.

That money only goes so far, however, when prices rise incessantly.

There has been plenty written about the K-shaped economy, where high- and low-income earners feel dramatically differently about their spending power. Yet it seems that nearly all Americans across the income spectrum are feeling the pinch of persistently higher gas prices on top of years of inflation. They're just handling it in different ways.

Consumers are unhappy with price increases, and still retail sales climb higher and higher even when adjusted for inflation. With the job market holding relatively steady, there haven't been major pullbacks in consumer spending.

However, wages haven't kept up the pace with inflation in recent months, writes LPL Chief Economist Jeffrey Roach. That impacts lower-earning Americans more, since they have less of a financial cushion. But even those in a position to splash out aren't inclined to do so, Roach notes.

"Households say jobs are harder to find, expect weaker income six months from now, and see business conditions deteriorating. Fewer openings and tougher job-hunting have people feeling as gloomy as they did in early 2021...plans to buy a home, a vehicle, or a major appliance have declined from prior months."

Holiday shopping intentions tell a similar story.

A survey by Teneo found that lower- and middle-income households plan to cut their holiday spending by at least 20%. Higher-income earners, who have theoretically enjoyed healthy stock market gains, are planning to hold their spending steady. That is better than slashing budgets, but not as ebullient as expected. A majority of respondents across income cohorts said they were looking for deals. Value is key.

New research by Bernstein analyst Zhihan Mausing, who used traffic and demographic data from Advan, shows more of the same: Both high- and low-income Americans have changed their habits.

"The short answer is that low income consumers are shopping more frequently - with smaller baskets - in value channels (especially in nearby dollar stores to save on gas)," she writes. "Meanwhile, for higher income consumers who can afford to buy larger baskets online, they are likely turning more to e-commerce rather than trading down in the brick and mortar channel amid ongoing gas inflation."

Ma found that visits to Walmart remained in the mid-single digit range despite a modest slowdown "perhaps as elevated gas prices weigh on lower income customers' willingness to drive to a Walmart," she posits.

If higher gas prices relent, that could be a catalyst for growth for Walmart and other retailers no matter which income band they cater to.

Costco Wholesale, which tends to cater to shoppers higher up the income scale, saw its visits accelerate in the second and third quarter, likely driven by its cheaper gas offerings.

"Target showed the strongest sequential improvement, with visits growth accelerating to the high-single digit range...supported by Target's improved merchandising and in-store experience," she writes. Target is in the midst of a turnaround focused on bringing shoppers back with better merchandising that has helped it sidestep some of the broader retail pain this year.

Visits to Dollar Tree and Dollar General are both positive year over year, although the latter has seen its traffic decelerate throughout the year. However she cautions that investors shouldn't extrapolate too much from this, given Dollar General's expanding partnerships with DoorDash, UberEats and Instacart. Inflationary pressure has been a double-edged sword for these deep discounters. Higher prices have weighed on core, lower-income consumers, while leading to some higher-income shoppers trading down.

"Overall, the U.S. consumer has remained resilient but value seeking," Ma concludes. "Should gas inflation start to moderate, this could weigh on dollar stores' traffic but help basket size, while Walmart could see improved in-store traffic as people are more inclined to drive."

When gas prices — currently around $4.30, near spring highs — start to moderate is anyone's guess.

data.title: Brazilian assets rise as investors await pivotal election
data.description:
Key points:
  • Brazilian assets steady ahead of Sunday election
  • Colombia peso up nearly 1%, government cuts spending budget
  • Venezuelans call for elections in first national protest in nearly two years
  • Mexican economy exceeds expectations in August

By Sudeshna Ghoshal and Johann M Cherian

Brazilian stocks rose on Friday as investors geared up for the presidential runoff in Latin America's largest economy, while the currency hit its highest in more than a week.

Voters will decide between right-wing candidate Senator Flavio Bolsonaro and incumbent President Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva on Sunday. Bolsonaro had performed better than expected earlier in the month, but recent polls have shown his lead over Lula was narrowing, sparking volatility in local markets.

The real has rallied 3.4% this month, marking its biggest monthly gain since April, while local stocks have advanced 10.3%, on course for their strongest month since January, on expectations that the senator would adopt fiscal consolidation policies if he won.

However, analysts said he was yet to offer clarity on the subject.

On Friday, the currency rose 0.9% against the dollar, while stocks were little changed. International bonds (105756CN8=), (105756BY5=) were marginally higher, while the equity benchmark rose 0.6%.

Ahead of the vote, data showed consumer inflation rose less-than-expected in the month to mid-October.

"Brazil is at the verge of fiscal dominance dynamics, and anything that improves the fiscal situation can lower risk premia," said Alejandro Cuadrado, managing director, global head FX & LatAm Strategy at BBVA.

"Lower risk premia implies the central bank can find more room to cut, lower interest rates, imply better valuations for Brazilian equities and potential growth and that brings flows from the offshore into Brazil."

MSCI indexes tracking regional equities (.MILA00000PUS) and currencies (.MILA00000CUS) rose 1.2% and 0.6%, respectively.

Brent crude prices rose over 3% after Houthi attacks in Saudi Arabia stoked concerns over further disruption to energy supplies from the Middle East.

Oil exporter Colombia's peso appreciated the most among regional currencies. It was last up nearly 1% after hitting a near one-month high.

Public finances were also in focus as the country's government cut this year's spending budget by 13.8 trillion pesos ($4.33 billion), although it was smaller than previously announced.

The Mexican peso inched up 0.2% against the dollar, but eyed its seventh straight week of losses, hit by expectations of a narrowing of the US-Mexico interest rate differential and uncertainty over the USMCA free trade deal.

Data showed the region's second largest economy grew more than expected in August from the prior month, with all three main sectors posting gains, official data showed.

Elsewhere, Venezuelans took to the streets on Thursday in the first nationwide opposition protest in nearly two years, as demonstrators demanded free elections and other political changes, with a notably thin presence of security forces.

The country's legacy international maturities were marginally higher.

Meanwhile, US first lady Melania Trump secured a ceasefire between Russia and Ukraine in the Russian-controlled city of Oleshky, which will begin on October 29, the White House said.

Kyiv's hard currency bonds (XS2895057334=TE), (XS2895056369=TE) gained over a cent following the news.

data.title: Former LPL Advisor Pleads Guilty to Fraud in Scheme That Cost Firms $3.3 Million — Barrons.com
data.description:
By Kenneth Corbin

A barred former investment advisor and broker has pleaded guilty to wire fraud in connection with a scheme that prosecutors say cost three financial services companies more than $3.3 million. Andrew Komarow, 37, of Avon, Conn., had initially pleaded not guilty to 11 charges, but entered a guilty plea to a lone count in federal court on Thursday.

Reached by email, Komarow didn't immediately provide a comment on the case. His lawyer didn't immediately respond to a request for comment.

Prosecutors say the fraud occurred between October 2022 and February 2023, when Komarow obtained lines of credit from three financial services companies and initiated nearly $9 million worth of transfers from his bank accounts to various brokerage accounts in his name. He executed those transactions knowing that he didn't have sufficient funds to support the transfers.

Komarow exploited a delay in the time between initiating those transfers and when the financial services firms posted and cleared them. He would then "conduct high-risk, short-term options trading in an attempt to make immediate profits to cover his insufficient funds," according to the Justice Department.

The financial services firms lost $3.35 million through the scheme, prosecutors say.

Komarow, who has autism, had been a widely cited expert on issues around neurodiversity and wealth management. He had been involved with the Financial Planning Association's efforts to support neurodivergent advisors and founded Planning Across the Spectrum, a now-defunct wealth management firm focused on special-needs planning.

Komarow first registered as a broker in 2010 with Pruco Securities and moved to LPL Financial in 2016. Later that year he registered as an investment advisor with Private Advisory Group, a large advisor firm affiliated with LPL.

By late 2022, the companies he worked for had caught on to Komarow's money-transfer scheme. Private Advisory Group terminated him in November of that year and LPL cut him loose in December, according to registration records.

Komarow was also on the radar of state and federal regulators. Finra, the brokerage industry's self-regulatory authority, barred Komarow from associating with any broker in June 2023. Connecticut securities regulators barred him from the industry in January 2024, and the Securities and Exchange Commission barred him in February 2024.

In the criminal case, the wire fraud charge carries a maximum sentence of 20 years in prison. The court hasn't scheduled Komarow's sentencing.
